title: Hallmark
direction: Editorial authority: a custom high-contrast lowercase serif word whose i-dot is a struck lozenge, the maker's punch, echoed as one wedge cut on every stem of the k-i-l run.
rationale: The name contains 'mark'; a hallmark is the small punched mark a maker strikes into finished work. An identity studio's own mark should look like a monograph from a great design press, not a generator.
semantics: lozenge = the punch / hallmark; three wedge-cut stems = deliberate
struck rhythm; oxblood = sealing wax / assay mark; bone paper = print

pitch.idea: A maker's mark for a studio that makes marks: the word markilo set like a monograph title, every stem cut with one 45-degree chisel and the i dotted with an oxblood lozenge, and a symmetric serif M that points to the same lozenge, struck like a hallmark.
strengths: Every letter carries one logic (chisel-notched stems, lozenge terminals), so it reads as lettering, not a font
the M icon is built from the word's stems, notch and lozenge and reads at 16 px
symmetric and calm, it works as an app icon, avatar and favicon
weaknesses: At 12-16 px the oxblood lozenge loses contrast against the ink
the i can read as a dotless Turkish ı
the icon is a letter, chosen by the owner over two drawn forms
